grammarFocus: 名词性从句入门；that 从句；情态动词与条件表达。
title: Smart Speaker, Smart Choices?
instructions: 本材料为模拟练习，非官方雅思试题。听录音前先读题，听两遍后作答。答案必须来自录音原文。
transcript:
Mia: Hi, Ben. You look worried. What's up?
Ben: Oh, hi Mia. It's my new smart speaker. I think it's great, but my sister says it listens to everything we say.
Mia: Well, that's partly true. Smart speakers only listen after they hear a wake word, like 'Hey Assistant'. But they do record what you say after that.
Ben: So if I say 'Hey Assistant, play music', it records that?
Mia: Yes, it saves the command. But the company says it deletes the recording after it answers. The problem is that some recordings are kept for improvement.
Ben: That's a bit scary. I don't want strangers hearing my private conversations.
Mia: I understand. You can turn off the microphone when you don't need it. And you can delete your voice history in the app.
Ben: Really? I didn't know that. But what if I forget to turn it off?
Mia: Then you should check the privacy settings. You can set it to delete recordings automatically after a week.
Ben: That sounds better. But my sister also said the speaker might share my data with other companies.
Mia: That depends on the company's policy. You should read the privacy notice. If they share data, they must tell you.
Ben: OK. I'll read it. But it's very long.
Mia: I know. Look for the parts about 'data sharing' and 'third parties'. If you can't find them, you can ask the company's support team.
Ben: Thanks, Mia. You know a lot about this.
Mia: I read a lot about technology. But I'm not an expert. I just try to be careful.
Ben: Me too. I think privacy is important. Maybe I'll write a short guide for my family.
Mia: That's a good idea. You could include a checklist: turn off the microphone, delete old recordings, and read the privacy notice.
Ben: I'll do that. Thanks for your help!
Mia: You're welcome. Let me know if you have more questions.

options: His new smart speaker might listen to private conversations.
His sister broke his smart speaker.
He cannot find the wake word for his smart speaker.
The smart speaker is too expensive.
answers: His new smart speaker might listen to private conversations.
questions.explanation: Ben 说“my sister says it listens to everything we say”，表明他担心智能音箱会监听私人对话。
questions.evidence: my sister says it listens to everything we say

questions.prompt: According to Mia, when do smart speakers start recording?
options: After they hear a wake word.
All the time, even when no one is speaking.
Only when you turn on the microphone.
When you open the app.
answers: After they hear a wake word.
questions.explanation: Mia 说“Smart speakers only listen after they hear a wake word”，即听到唤醒词后才开始录音。
questions.evidence: Smart speakers only listen after they hear a wake word

questions.prompt: What can Ben turn off when he doesn't need the smart speaker? (one word)
questions.explanation: Mia 建议“You can turn off the microphone when you don't need it”，因此答案是 microphone。
questions.evidence: You can turn off the microphone when you don't need it.

questions.prompt: What does Mia suggest Ben should do if he forgets to turn off the microphone?
options: Check the privacy settings.
Buy a new smart speaker.
Ask his sister for help.
Turn off the Wi-Fi.
questions.explanation: Mia 说“Then you should check the privacy settings”，所以答案是检查隐私设置。
questions.evidence: Then you should check the privacy settings.

questions.prompt: What does Ben's sister say about the smart speaker?
options: It might share his data with other companies.
It deletes all recordings automatically.
It is very easy to use.
It has a good privacy policy.
answers: It might share his data with other companies.
questions.explanation: Ben 说“my sister also said the speaker might share my data with other companies”，因此选此项。
questions.evidence: my sister also said the speaker might share my data with other companies

questions.prompt: What should Ben look for in the privacy notice?
options: Parts about 'data sharing' and 'third parties'.
The price of the smart speaker.
The name of the company's CEO.
The warranty information.
questions.explanation: Mia 建议“Look for the parts about 'data sharing' and 'third parties'”，因此选此项。
questions.evidence: Look for the parts about 'data sharing' and 'third parties'.

questions.prompt: Mia says she is an expert in technology.
options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: Mia 明确说“I'm not an expert”，因此“Mia says she is an expert”是错误的。

questions.prompt: Ben's sister owns a smart speaker.
options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: 录音中只提到 Ben 的姐姐说智能音箱会监听，但没有说她是否拥有智能音箱。因此该信息未给出。
questions.evidence: 录音中没有提到 Ben 的姐姐是否拥有智能音箱。

questions.prompt: What does Ben want to write for his family? (one word)
questions.explanation: Ben 说“Maybe I'll write a short guide for my family”，因此答案是 guide。
questions.evidence: Maybe I'll write a short guide for my family.

questions.prompt: What does Mia suggest Ben could include in his guide?
options: A checklist with three actions.
A list of smart speaker brands.
A phone number for the company.
A warning about Wi-Fi.
questions.explanation: Mia 说“You could include a checklist: turn off the microphone, delete old recordings, and read the privacy notice”，即一个包含三项行动的清单。
questions.evidence: You could include a checklist: turn off the microphone, delete old recordings, and read the privacy notice.

vocabulary.example: My new smart speaker can play music.
You need to say the wake word first.
You can delete your voice history.
Privacy is important to many people.
Check the privacy settings in the app.
The company's policy explains data sharing.
Make a checklist before you travel.

grammar.title: 名词性从句入门；that 从句；情态动词与条件表达
grammar.explanation: 名词性从句在句子中充当名词成分，例如主语、宾语或表语。that 从句常作宾语，that 可省略。情态动词如 should, can, might 表示建议、能力或可能性。条件表达常用 if 引导条件句，主句用情态动词。
grammar.example: You should check the privacy settings. If they share data, they must tell you.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a that-clause.
options: I think that privacy is important.
I think privacy is important that.
That I think privacy is important.
I think what privacy is important.
answers: I think that privacy is important.
questions.explanation: that 从句作 think 的宾语，that 可省略，但位置应在动词后。
questions.evidence: I think that privacy is important.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a modal verb.
options: You should to read the privacy notice.
You should read the privacy notice.
You should reading the privacy notice.
You should reads the privacy notice.
answers: You should read the privacy notice.
questions.explanation: 情态动词 should 后接动词原形，不加 to，也不加 -ing 或 -s。
questions.evidence: You should read the privacy notice.

options: If you forget to turn it off, you should check the settings.
If you forget to turn it off, you should checking the settings.
If you forget to turn it off, you should to check the settings.
If you forget to turn it off, you should checks the settings.
answers: If you forget to turn it off, you should check the settings.
questions.explanation: if 引导条件从句，主句用情态动词 should + 动词原形。
questions.evidence: If you forget to turn it off, you should check the settings.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a that-clause as object.
options: She said that she would delete the recordings.
She said that would delete the recordings.
She said delete the recordings that.
She said what she would delete the recordings.
answers: She said that she would delete the recordings.
questions.explanation: that 从句作 said 的宾语，从句需有完整主语和谓语。
questions.evidence: She said that she would delete the recordings.

part2Bullets: and explain why you made that choice
